utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Call the case, please, Madam Court Deputy.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-01-48-T, the Prosecutor versus Sefer Halilovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Today we'll continue the examination of this witness, and after that, if we have time, we might have a discussion on the procedural matters. Yes, Mr. Morrissey. Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just indicate the Prosecution was able to locate yesterday one of the documents - I think it was MFI196 - that Mr. Morrissey put to the witness. It's the command and control JNA book -- manual which has been translated. I think it's in its entirety. We've provided copies electronically to the registry, Chambers, and to my learned friends.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We might have the opportunity to deal with this issue at a later stage. Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I confirm that I received the document that is indicated by Mr. Re. I'm grateful for the Prosecutor's assistance in that regard. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now -- sorry, Mr. Cikotic. I just want to turn to another area of military doctrine, and that's -- it's really an expert opinion or an opinion from somebody who -- who practiced in the field that I ask you this question. You've already been asked some questions about the -- the situation of a Chief of Staff. Now I want to ask you now some questions about deputy commanders and the way in which a deputy commander might sign an order when they sign an order. First of all, I'll just ask a couple of general questions: Is it the fact that in the situation where a commander gives an order to the deputy to exercise command power, even combat command power, then the deputy may, given that order by the commander, exercise such power? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: In circumstances like that, it's customary or it's the practice for a deputy commander to sign the order using the word "zastupa" z-a-s-t-u-p-a; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Would you just excuse me. I'm just going to show you a couple of examples of this so that the Tribunal can see how this works in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, we're just going to find the right number to -- this is a document that's already in evidence. Yes. Could the witness please be shown MFI160 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: While this is being produced, Mr. Cikotic, this is an order you may not have seen, and I don't presume that you have seen it. I'm really going to ask you to comment on the -- the signing practice of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I think the witness should be shown, please, page 2 of the document in B/C/S so that he can see the words at the end of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, we have some, you know, technical problem, that is, that we could not have the English version on the screen, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: For the purpose of this cross-examination, that may not pose a problem because I'm really seeking just to draw the Tribunal's attention to the -- actually, to the B/C/S word and then have the witness explain in the best way that he can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: On the screen now is the front page of a particular order dated the 16th of the 9th, 1993. Just to be clear about this, can you recall whether or not you've actually seen this particular order before?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Nevertheless, I'll still show you the following page to ask you to comment on the formula that's used.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could we please see the ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, if there be a technical problem, Mr. Cengic is going to fetch the original document and it can be shown on the ELMO because, as I say, it's not about the substance of the document but its form that I'm -- that I'm questioning the witness. I'll move on to another topic until that's done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Sorry, Mr. Cikotic. That miscarried. Very well. Mr. -- while we're waiting for that to be done, I'm just going to ask you some further questions about the -- the meeting at Dobro Polje on the 5th of September. Can you indicate approximately -- only -- doing the best you can with your memory, how long that meeting lasted for?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it could have lasted an hour or two.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in terms of the tasks that were assigned, I'm going to now ask you some questions about the arrows that are drawn on the map there. On the map that you were shown, did the directions indicated for the various units correspond -- or perhaps I'll ask you about your experience first. The directions indicated on that map corresponded to plans which essentially you had already considered over the preceding weeks as an appropriate way to proceed on your axis; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. And to the extent that you can comment about this, in the areas of the 6th Corps responsibility that were near to you, were you aware that the 6th Corps had themselves already drafted -- sorry, I shouldn't say "drafted" -- but had already considered attacks in those areas even before this meeting at Dobro Polje?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so, but I don't know and I can't claim with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's okay. Well, if that's the case, I won't press you about it. But certainly at Dobro Polje nothing new was added to that map that's behind you there but, rather, what happened was that that map was explained and details about it were explained to those who actually had to do the fighting. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mostly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And after that time, after you went back to your -- your command, you never did meet with Sefer Halilovic in person again during the time, well, before he was arrested on the 26th of October of 1993; is that accurate?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you personally were not present at any discussions between Commander Delic and Chief of Staff Halilovic which preceded the meeting at Dobro Polje; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Did you personally see Commander Delic the day before the Dobro Polje meeting when it appears he came to Jablanica and to Konjic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. And were you aware that Commander Delic sometimes in the course of -- well, perhaps I should ask you this: In the week following the Dobro Polje meeting, did you become aware that Commander Delic was at one stage in the city of Zenica, which was in the 3rd Corps zone of responsibility?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, there's a document I want to show you which you may or may not have seen. I'll show it to you and then I'm going to ask you some questions about -- about its form as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, please, Mr. Cikotic, while we locate the document which is going to be shown to you on the screen. While that's being searched for, I now notice that the lost document from earlier has now appeared. And because that's a short topic, I might -- although it's unsequential, I might jump back to it now while it's tonne screen. Mr. Cikotic, do you now have on the screen the second page of that document, which appears to be signed by Stjepan Siber?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, I'm not concerned with the content of the document, but could you just read into the transcript the words used and the title used in the signature by Mr. Siber at the bottom right of that document.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, what -- are the words that are used there "zastupa komandanta"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's that is what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what's the meaning of the word "zastupa" as it's used there in that document?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that he is acting on behalf of the commander as his representative in signing this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And as a result of signing the document in that way, that means that the order is a binding order to those it's directed to; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Morrissey, are you going to tender this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I -- well, it's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, and I'm really just asking the witness to comment on the form that's used there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the witness please be shown now a document, MFI161.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Do you have that document in the Bosnian language in front of you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But could it be zoomed in so that I could read the text?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness please have it zoomed in, and in particular the part I want to show you is the bottom right, the signature area.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Do you notice that this document is signed -- at least -- it may not be signed, but it's got the title of the name "Sefer Halilovic" under it under the heading of "nacalnik" but also using the term "zamjenik komandanta". Do you see that both terms are used there?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, just to be clear, and to your understanding, Sefer Halilovic was indeed the Chief of the General Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, was it also your understanding that -- you may or may not know the answer to this, but if you do, please tell us -- that the -- after the order of the 18th of July, 1993 the Chief of Staff was ex officio one of the three deputy commanders of the Bosnian army, that being one Croat, one Serb, and one Bosniak person? Was that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this is how it was interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And just to be clear, I -- I don't want to misrepresent your position. Do you remember whether or not you actually saw that order of the 18th of July which -- which brought about that ex officio state of affairs?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't see the order.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. In signing this document with the words "Chief of Staff" in capital letters and then the words "zamjenik komandanta" in small letters in brackets and without using the word "zastupa"," would you agree that -- would you interpret this as -- as a -- a letter and an order indeed that's signed by Sefer Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: If it was being signed by him in his capacity as deputy commander, you would expect him to use the term "zastupa"; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: There's one more document that I -- both of these documents were tendered at an earlier time by the Prosecutor and I just want to put both of them to you. So that was MFI161. Could the witness now be shown MFI123.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And I'm going to go through the same process in asking you questions about this document as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And perhaps, Your Honours, while that's being brought up, could I just indicate the context of this questioning is that you may recall in cross -- in re-examination of the witness Salko Gusic, he having been questioned about whether Mr. Halilovic acted as deputy or as Chief of Staff. Learned counsel for the Prosecutor, Ms. Chana at the time, put these two documents to him because each has the -- the word "zamjenik" there, and so I'm seeking to clarify how that operates by this questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you now have before you another document which once again is under the name of Sefer Halilovic in the bottom right-hand corner, signed as Chief of -- of the General Staff, but with the words "deputy commander" in brackets? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And do you agree with me that, as with the last document, that appears to be signed by Halilovic in his capacity as Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that if he was signing in his capacity as deputy commander, you would have expected to see the word "zastupa" used? Is that also correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. I've completed those -- those documents. There's one other document that I want to put to you. This is Defence document that should be in the system now. This is unrelated to those matters and this is a document that appears to pass through the 3rd Corps. I wish to ask you about that. It's document -- Defence document DD00.2468. It should be MFI201. And I will offer it for tender through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, could I just ask you: Do you have in front of you now a document with the handwritten words "D535" in the top right-hand corner?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a document here, number 535.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, just excuse me one moment, Mr. Cikotic. I want to say something to the Court about this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, this document has been accessed from the archives, and it will be apparent on the face of it that the photocopy accessed by the Defence has got two orders on it. And so that the Prosecutor can be clear and so that the Court can be clear as well, you'll see that the top order ceases about halfway down the page, and thereafter is to be found an unrelated order upon which I'm not relying, but it's included there because we didn't want to be editing the -- what we found. So it's evident that what's being taken from the archives is a -- a photocopied document which has got two documents on it. I'm relying on the first and not on the second, but I think that should be pointed out, that there is another document, an unrelated one there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And this document did not appear on the list you submitted to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: No, I can indicate that the decision to -- to refer to it was taken probably 20 minutes before we came to court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: And how about the translation? Who did the translation of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's -- it's been translated long ago, and it's -- it's been in Defence possession for a long time. The decision to put it through this witness has -- was taken right now. And the reason will be evident when I -- when I ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: It's a -- pardon me, Your Honour, but the answer to your question is it's a CLSS translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, first of all, this order -- or sorry, this letter or request here is a letter that is under the hand of Zulfikar Alispago, Zuka, and it's addressed to Commander Rasim Delic personally, and it's headed the "3rd Corps" -- now -- and dated the 15th of December, 1993. Now, my question is first of all is: What reason might there be for a letter to be addressed to Rasim Delic of the 3rd Corps. And you'll recall I asked you a question earlier on about Commander Delic being as Zenica. You said you didn't recall, you didn't know. But are you able to explain how such a letter may be addressed to the 3rd Corps when it seems to be addressed to Commander Rasim Delic personally?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the command of the 3rd Corps was the closest communications centre that could convey letter, this document, to Commander Rasim Delic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps I -- perhaps if I could just ask you this: In the real world of the battlefield, was it the case that because commanders sometimes moved around, they had to be chased to various command posts in order to get messages to them?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, does that appear to you, that document there, to be a simple combat report with an additional specific request concerning a helicopter?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As far as I can read it here, because it's not really legible, I believe that's what it's about.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I don't want you to be put in a bad position about this. Would it assist if the zoom function was used to help you look at it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Could the witness have that done, please.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see the entire document now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Well, just perhaps if you're able to comment -- if you look at the top of it and then when you've exhausted that, then ask that it -- ask that it be moved down and the Court staff will assist you in doing that. Mr. Cikotic, have you read as much as you can read of it now?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Do you need the screen to be adjusted in any way now?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, can you confirm that what you have there is a combat report from Zulfikar Alispago to Commander Delic on the 15th of September, 1993 which contains an additional request for a helicopter to help some wounded soldiers?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. And as far as you can see, that passed through the communications centre of the 3rd Corps, a member of which you were?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I offer that document for tender, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, any objections?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The Prosecution's concern about the tender of this particular document is this is probably not the correct witness to tender that document through. It's a document written extensively by Mr. Alispago Zulfikar to Rasim Delic personally. Now, the witness is entitled to comment upon the order in general -- sorry, the report in general terms, but what's the basis of tendering it through him? What's the basis of tendering it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Morrissey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, the link is the 3rd Corps communications centre, this -- this witness being a member of the 3rd Corps and it being his organisation through which -- through which the document came. It's a little difficult to deal with the Prosecutor's objection because both Rasim Delic and Zulfikar Alispago were both Prosecution witnesses until one month ago, both of them having been withdrawn at a very late stage by the Prosecutors. Now, that's within their prerogative. They've sought leave of the court and that leave has been granted and we don't seek to traverse that. But on any view, this document is plainly relevant and directly relevant to the command responsibilities and the answerabilty of Mr. Zulfikar Alispago to Commander Rasim Delic. It's just a clearly relevant document. In all the circumstances, if there was any genuine challenge to its -- to its authenticity, that might be a different thing, but my learned friend doesn't raise that objection and rightly not. And because it's passed through the 3rd Corps, because it's a military document, because it's in the archives, in my submission unless there was something about it that rendered its provenance important or -- or difficult or significant, then this witness is the only witness in the Prosecution case through whom it should be tendered, because he's from the 3rd Corps and it's not suggested that he personally saw it, but he can indicate how it arrived in -- in -- if you like, in typical terms, which he has done.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I withdraw the objection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: As the Court pleases.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thank you very much, Mr. Re. In my view, the contents of this document is totally irrelevant [Realtime transcript read in error "relevant"] to our case. But you tender it because of the form and the chain of the transmission of the document. So we'll have it admitted into the evidence. And the court deputy will announce a number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This document will be Defence Exhibit D201.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Could I just clarify something? I thought I heard Your Honour say the document is totally irrelevant. Did Your Honour say "relevant" or "totally irrelevant"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: I mean the contents. As for asking for the helicopters -- all this has nothing to do with our case, so in this way I believe it's irrelevant to our case. But the Defence tenders this document not only for the contents of this document. More important is for the chain of the transmission and the commander's responsibility, you know, here is involved. So we believe in this aspect it's relevant. Based on this reason, we admit it into the evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My clarification was only because the transcript said "totally relevant" and I thought I heard Your Honour say "irrelevant."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Oh. Okay. Thank you very much. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Sorry, I'm just reminded, Your Honour, that -- no, I'll deal with the matter later. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cikotic. That's the -- those are the questions about the -- the deputy situation. Now, I just wish to move now to what happened after Dobro Polje. It was the fact that you awaited a signal of some sort to commence your part of the operation at the northern end of this line of -- of military operations; is that the case?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to ask you some questions about the -- the timing and the way that this operation unfolded.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And, first of all, I just want to witness to be shown the document MFI149. This is a document that has not yet been admitted into evidence but the Prosecution have indicated they don't oppose it being admitted. It's one of the documents that was put to Commander -- Commander Gusic by the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just as it's being brought up on the screen, Mr. Cikotic, I'll explain that it's a report by the commander of the Independent Prozor Battalion, Enver Buza. Now, do you have before you -- I'm sorry, do you have before you now in Bosnian a copy of -- or this report?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Please just excuse me a moment while I -- I've got a marked copy which I want to put to you. I've taken it out. My apologies for that. Is that a report that appears to you -- and take as much time as you need to look at the report. Does it appear to you to be a document addressed to the 6th Corps command and emanating from the Prozor Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a report of the Prozor Independent Battalion commander to the commander of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And could I just ask you to direct your attention to the very first paragraph, where it commences: "Pursuant to attack order, operative number 01/1500-27 of the 11th of the 9th, 1993." Do you see that passage?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could you just explain to the Tribunal why it is that a report like this might refer to the number of an operative order, as this one appears to do.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a combat report, and I believe that this implies that the task has been accomplished as defined in the report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And by referring to the order operative number, the writer of this report is indicating that the tasks accomplished were accomplished pursuant to that particular order; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Very well. Now, does this order indicate to you that -- and this is on -- it's still in that first paragraph -- that "The Prozor Independent Battalion infiltrated enemy territory on the night between the 13th and the 14th of September"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that -- and now, I'm not sticking to one paragraph here, but generally speaking in the follow-up paragraphs does the writer of this report indicate that combat activities thereafter took place in the morning following that infiltration?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that would make sense after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thanks. Just excuse me -- can I ask you please, Mr. Cikotic, to indicate: Is that whole report in the Bosnian language contained on one page in the screen in front of you, or is it divided into two pages?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Good.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, could I just indicate to the Court, Your Honours, the English translation is in two parts, so it may be that the -- the Court will need to turn over the page here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But if you -- I won't turn over the page yet, so if we just stay where we are. But I indicate I'm going to -- I'm sorry, the court staff anticipated me there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Would it be possible to go back to the previous page in English. Thank you. And we'll go back to a moment. But just now I want to take you to a couple aspects of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, do you notice there's a -- a paragraph there that says the following words: "The following units participated in the attack, two platoons of the 1st Company, two platoons of the 2nd Company, one platoon to the 3rd Company, one of the 4th Company, the military police, part of the Prozor MUP forces," and then it goes on to refer to other company commanders and so on. Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Were -- was it very common that the -- now, the MUP, the M-U-P, that's the civilian police, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask you this: When the MUP were used, when the M-U-P, the civilian police, were used in an operation, did there have to be a specific subordination of those units to the army commander before the army commander was able to command them? And my question is really a general one, from your knowledge. I appreciate you weren't in Uzdol yourself.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be the unit commander from the MUP who would command the MUP unit, but they were subordinated to the BiH army within the scope of that action that they participated in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And how would they be resubordinated? Would it be by an order? And if so, who had -- who had to issue such an order before the police were -- the civilian police were resubordinated to the army?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depended on the resubordination level. In any case, it had to be somebody who had the authority to carry out such resubordination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And -- and that order -- the order that was given to the MUP units to be resubordinated to the army had to come from someone inside the Ministry of the Interior; is that correct? In other words, one of their own commanders had to resubordinate them before they could cross over.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in principle that would be the case. However, I believe that in real situations MUP units were engaged based on the agreement between the Prozor MUP and the Prozor Independent Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in such situations, what you'd have is -- well, you tell me. I won't put words in your mouth. You tell me. But in a situation like that, you would have MUP units fighting alongside army units without the army units having -- without the army commander having any formal power to command those units; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander of the military unit who is in charge of the operation will also command the MUP unit that is involved in that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. But if there's no specific legal resubordination of the MUP unit to the army, then the commander doesn't have any legal power to command that unit; is that accurate or is that artificial?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, the -- perhaps the question should be -- could be clarified. My learned friend has used the word "legal subordination." As the Trial Chamber is, of course, aware, subordination or effective control can be de facto or de jure. So the use of the word "legal" is perhaps misleading in the context where the Prosecution is in fact alleging a combination of both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: To my understanding, "legal" means according to the rules of the army. You know, maybe that should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that was the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: But -- but I don't think we should confuse the witness with the specific, you know, legal terms, like the de facto, de jure. You know, it sounds strange to the -- to a layman, you know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I agree. But the witness is competent to comment upon the rules of the army, and that's really what I was asking him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, just so that -- so that my question doesn't mislead anyone in the court, what I'm putting to you when I say -- when I use the term "legal," I mean according to the rules of the army as you understood them to be. Now, I'll just -- I'll come back to my question in that context. In the absence of a specific order of resubordination to the MUP units, is it the fact that the army commander doesn't have any power under the rules to command the MUP units?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And just to come to the specific concrete case here, you personally cannot comment on whether Enver Buza in fact had any power, de facto or de jure, over the Prozor civilian police that are said to have joined in the attack here; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I just want to take you to the -- to the end of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And could the English translation be turned over, please, to the following page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Having regard to the -- do you notice that there's a -- a paragraph there: "Conclusion. This report and the overall data have been made available to the Seveka [phoen] -- sorry, SVK chief, Sefer Halilovic, Colonel Vehbija Karic, and Colonel Zikrija Suljevic, who monitored the whole operation from the observation post," and signed Commander Buza. To your understanding, given Sefer Halilovic's function of the coordination of this operation, it was necessary for Enver Buza to send a copy of -- of combat reports such as this to Sefer Halilovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If he was on the strength of the 6th Corps, it would have sufficed for him to send his report to the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, it's apparent here that he sent the report to -- sent this combat report to the command of the 6th Corps but that he has also made the overall data available to Sefer Halilovic. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And you also agree that the order to which Buza refers in the very first paragraph is given an identifying number so that we can find out exactly which order Buza was obeying when he went into battle by reference to that number?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, could the witness please be shown -- there's another document -- well, I'm going to show you that -- that document now. Could the witness please be shown MFI152.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And here again, as the -- as the document is being brought up, Mr. Cikotic, I'll make it clear I'm not going to ask you to comment on -- on anything here other than the form of the document and -- and the number on it in particular. Do you now have in front of you the Bosnian version of a particular order to attack?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And do you see that that order to attack has been given an operation number, namely the same one that was on the other document, the Buza document, 01/1500-27?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And this appears to you to be -- sorry, the process between those two letters is what I'm asking you about -- or this -- this order and the report. I'll start that question again because it got lost. It's quite apparent to you that the report of Buza is referring to this order here, which has the number on it at the top; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Very well. Those are the questions about those documents. Now, I just want to ask you some narrative questions about what actually happened at around the time of the start of the attack. You personally at a distance of 11 and a half years do not recall the precise date of the attack that you launched; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But what you can say is that you went into battle in cooperation with the 317th Brigade under Enver Zejnilagic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And what you can say is that on the first day of that operation, you achieved your objective, which was the occupation of the village of Vilica Guvno; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: The troops of Zejnilagic were tasked to occupy a particular high hill named Crni Vrh; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was not Zejnilagic's task. He may have assisted somebody else, but I believe that this was the task of the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. The units of the 6th Corps which were tasked to occupy Crni Vrh, to your knowledge initially succeeded in doing so on the first day of that operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, on the first day they were not engaged in the expected activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, what we have in this case is -- well, perhaps I'll put the questions another way. Do you recall that those who were tasked to occupy that area were not assisted, as they should have been, by the Prozor Independent Battalion on that -- on the first day of their operations?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The situation in that part of the front line was not clear at the time, but I know that they did not advance in that area, as it was ordered and as it was expected.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, and when you say "they did not advance," what you heard about that was that it was the Prozor Independent Battalion under Enver Buza who did not advance as he was expected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm primarily referring to the Prozor Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And I understand you were busy doing your task in your area, but according to the intelligence that you received and the -- the battlefront news that you received, was it the case that you heard that the Prozor Independent Battalion was then told that they had to perform their task and they were ordered to do so overnight and the morning of the following day? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I received information that there would be some delay in the accomplishment of his task but that he would do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. And then on the -- you've seen that the Prozor Independent Battalion commander indicates that he infiltrated on the night of the 13th and fought on the -- on the morning of the 14th in the hamlet of Uzdol. And what I want to ask you is: You've got no reason to doubt the accuracy of that particular date, have you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Working backwards from that, if the Prozor Independent Battalion went into action belatedly on the morning of the 14th, does that mean that your unit went into action the day before that, on the 13th, or did you go into action two days before that, on the 12th?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that we're talking about one day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Okay. And I appreciate that you don't have a note of the date, of which day it was, but it would appear to you, bearing in mind the Buza report and what you know of the -- of the incidents, that on the 13th of -- of September troops at the northern end of that line on the map went into battle, with the exception of the Prozor Independent Battalion, and then on the 14th the Prozor Independent Battalion belatedly went into action. Does that appear to reflect the true situation now that you've had a look at the report and given the evidence that you have given?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that this would have been the case in the northern part.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Now, subsequently to the Prozor Independent Battalion going to Uzdol -- well, I withdraw that. To your knowledge, the troops which were supposed to be supported by -- by Buza and the Prozor Independent Battalion in fact were unable to hold onto the mountain Crni Vrh; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And effectively that was because the flank of that mountain was exposed to fire by the HVO; whereas, the plan had been that the HVO in that sector were to be distracted by Buza; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume that that was the case; however, the details escape me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. Just so that the Tribunal has a grasp of what the ABiH strategy was: In those days, the HVO had a marked advantage over you in terms of tanks, shells, and materiel equipment; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And the advantage that you had was that you had a superiority in manpower and a possible superiority in knowledge of the terrain by your soldiers.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No audible response]

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you'll have to say yes or no, because it's recording.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Thanks. So that generally speaking the strategy of -- of the Bosnian army at that place was to attack in a coordinated way on many small fronts.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And in that way, to distract the HVO and to stretch their forces as thinly as you could do.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But that required very good staffwork and coordination at a higher level in order to make sure that the attacks all happened at the same time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that was the need to have Sefer Halilovic, Zucro Suljevic, Rifat Bilajac, and Vehbija Karic performing that coordinating role because it needed experienced cool heads who had been in battle and had experience in battle; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, just excuse me a moment. I've --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I've finished with that document now, Madam Court Deputy. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, you indicated, Mr. Cikotic, that you accomplished your tasks effectively within the first two to three days of the operation; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And thereafter, you were concerned -- your job was effectively to hold onto the area which you had occupied; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And that area included a number of villages which were formally occupied but were not empty; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In this particular area, there were no inhabited settlements.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I was going to ask you -- there was no inhabited settlement as Vilica Guvno?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vilica Guvno is not a village. It's a feature on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I understand. My apologies. Yes, well,--

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Could the transcript reveal that that was counsel's mistake about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Cikotic. Very well. Now, could I just continue about what happened after that. If it be assumed that your attack took -- and that's using the detective work that we've used, working backwards from Buza's order and so on. If it be assumed that you attacked on the 13th, would you say that your -- your own forces' offensive operations came to a stop around the 15th or the 16th approximately?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The offensive stopped during the first day, and in the course of the second day there were mostly defensive activities taking place in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: I see. Because the HVO, using a nonmilitary term, were not very happy about your victory and they tried to chase you off again; is that true?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Now, I understand you were not -- one thing we can be clear about: You were not the commander of Operation Neretva 93. But you may be able to comment on your knowledge because you were on the ground at the time in that area. As far as you know, the effort to relieve Mostar continued right into 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, until the end of 1993 and early 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And in that time, to your recollection, operations as depicted upon the map there, the Operation Neretva map, continued to be attempted and continued to be put into place by the Bosnian army in that time with the view of liberating Mostar; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And those actions continued even after Sefer Halilovic was arrested on the 26th of October of 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: And to your knowledge, after the time that he was arrested on the 26th of October, 1993, you never heard of Sefer Halilovic performing any command role in the army after that time, did you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. The power to stop this particular operation, to put a stop to it, lay with two people, I suggest: Rasim Delic, as commander of the army and the signer of that map, and Alija Izetbegovic, as the head of the Presidency. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether Alija Izetbegovic commanded the operations directly, but Rasim Delic definitely did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Yes. And Rasim Delic had the power to stop this operation if that was the decision that he wanted to take; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: But Sefer Halilovic, the Chief of Staff of the operation -- sorry, the Chief of Staff of the General Staff, certainly did not have the power of his own motion or of his own decision to put a stop to this operation, did he?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: When I put that proposition to you about Alija Izetbegovic before, I -- I didn't mean to mislead you. Obviously he was not directly commanding combat operations. But to your understanding, was Alija Izetbegovic, as the head of the Bosnian Presidency, the Supreme Commander of all the armed forces in a formal sense?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Okay. Yes. Would you please just excuse me for a moment, please, Mr. Cikotic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, there may be a couple of small matters. I'd just like maybe a minute. I don't ask for an adjournment of the case. But I'd just like to consult briefly with Mr. Dzambasovic and with co-counsel, but I think I've effectively finished the cross-examining. Just excuse me a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, that's the cross-examination. Mr. Cikotic, thank you for your patience in answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Any redirect, Mr. Re?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, just on the last questions that Mr. Morrissey asked you, about Rasim Delic's role in Operation Neretva, did you have any personal knowledge about what Rasim Delic may or may not have done in relation to this operation, apart from appending his signature to the top left of the map, which is just behind you on that board?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no knowledge about his involvement in the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To clarify, your knowledge is confined to the fact that his signature is on -- is appended to the top left of the map headed "Operacija Neretva"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't want there to be any leading questions in redirect, and I object to that one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, thing is -- question was a follow-up question. This time, you are allowed, Mr. Re, to continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question was to clarify your previous answer, are you saying that your knowledge about Rasim Delic's role is confined to the fact that his signature is on the top of that map?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you a number of questions and showed you some documents signed by Mr. Halilovic in different capacities as Chief of Staff and as the deputy commander. From your position as the commander of an operational group within the 3rd Corps, if you had received an order from Sefer -- or a document purporting to be an order signed by Sefer Halilovic, either signed as the Chief of Staff or as the deputy commander of the ABiH, would you have obeyed that order?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there's an objection to the form of that question. My learned friend is indeed entitled to ask questions arising out of the cross-examination and in particular what he's referring to is a line of questions I asked clarifying what a signature of a deputy meant. And you'll recall it focussed on the use of the term "zastupa." Now, my learned friend may be entitled to ask the follow-up question on a different basis, but -- so I won't quibble about it, although it didn't really seem to follow. But the witness shouldn't be asked a speculative question. What he can be asked is: What would be the effect of an order signed by Halilovic in one capacity? What would be the effect of it being signed in another capacity? And using the term "deputy" there disguises the very issue I was asking about and which Mr. Re uses to base his question. So I don't object to questioning -- to clarify what this witness -- how this witness may have responded to a particular order. That's admissible. But I do object to the way that's phrased, as I've just said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I see no problem for the Prosecution to ask this question. You may proceed, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you remember and do you understand the question I asked you a moment ago, Mr. Cikotic?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember and I've understood it. I would obey an order signed by Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right. Would it make any difference -- would it have made any difference to you whether you would have obeyed the order had Mr. Halilovic signed it as either Chief of Staff or deputy commander of the ABiH? That was the essence of my question.

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I believe that it would have made very little difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Does that apply whether it was an oral or a written order?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you ever discuss at any time with Mr. Halilovic the capacity in which he would sign a document or an order, whether as deputy commander or as Chief of Staff?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday Mr. Morrissey showed you three JNA military books, the "Introduction to theory of military control," "The rule on the divisions of the land army," and one called "Rule on the corps." That's the translations which were read onto the record yesterday, and he read extracts to you which were of relating to JNA military doctrine and asked you about its applicability to the ABiH in 1993. He also asked you about operational groups and how they worked within the ABiH. Now, you had -- you've given evidence that you were a career JNA officer and had been in the JNA for, I think, seven years before you joined the ABiH. Was there any difference that you know of between an operational group under JNA military doctrine and an operational group in the fledgling ABiH in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my -- or rather, I was not familiar with the operations groups' terms under the JNA doctrine, because I didn't have occasion to study the doctrine prior to the war; however, since the BiH army doctrine to a certain extent was taken over from the JNA doctrine, I believe that the terms were interpreted in a similar fashion.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And when you say "in a similar fashion," are you referring to the size, the types of units which would be in an operational group, and the geography, the area which they could encompass?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, sorry, could I just intervene there. That is a leading question because it limits the sort of areas in which the similarities might exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Okay. I'll clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, I believe that it is a leading question, but in this context I regard it as a clarification on that. Maybe you could just ask a blunt question on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Just to make the question more general, to clarify your earlier answer when you said "in a similar fashion": Were you -- are you referring to the size, types of units which would be in an operational group, the geography, the area they would encompass, the type of command, or something else?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was mostly referring to the structure of the units, that numbered a certain number of men and that covered a certain area in which they were engaged.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also showed you a -- a document, which is MFI146, which referred to "inspection team." The date of the document was the 30th of August, 1993. Do you remember that document or do you want me to show it to you again? He asked you some questions at -- questions at some length about various parts of the document and the composition of what was called "the inspection team." Do you need to see it again or do you recall the document?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe I recall the contents of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question is this: Mr. Morrissey asked you a lot of questions about that document. When was the first time you ever saw that document?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it here three days ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Had you ever heard of the existence of that document before you came to The Hague earlier this week?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the past two or three years, I believe I had heard about the document being discussed. But at the relevant time, I didn't know of its existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about this term "inspection team"? Had you heard it discussed in the context of Mr. Halilovic being a member of a so-called inspection team in 1993?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember him representing his role this way. As far as I remember, he said that his role was to coordinate combat activities on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you aware of there being a specific military term within JNA or ABiH doctrine; namely, "inspection team"?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was such a term.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And encompassed within that term is -- is -- I withdraw that. Is the coordination of combat activities encompassed within the term "inspection team"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, sorry, there's an objection to that question. My learned friend ought to specify there whether he's asking the witness one of two questions: Is he asking the witness about inspection teams in the abstract as they're represented in manuals, in which case the witness can answer about that; or is he talking about this document and the inspection team that is confronted here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. We need some specifications in your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My question wasn't precise enough, Mr. Cikotic, and I apologise for that. I'm talking in the doctrinal sense. In the doctrinal sense, do you understand an inspection team or the term "inspection team" to include the coordination of combat activities, or do you -- or do you understand it to refer to some other function?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This all depends on what the specific task of the inspection team is. In principle, an inspection team could have very broad powers, including the dismissal of the core personnel and the engagement of troops in any sort of combat.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I just want you to elaborate on that slightly and I don't want to lead. In your experience and under doctrine, how wide or how many powers could an inspection team be given?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, I believe that this depends on the decision by the commander, or rather, by the authority that decides to set up and send an inspection team in the field.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: You just referred to the engagement of troops in any sort of combat. Does that also include the issuing of orders in combat?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I suppose that this is something that is defined within the role of the inspection team, which can include such powers too.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, Mr. Morrissey also asked you about -- specifically about MUP units and the use of MUP units in combat activities. Did OG Zapad ever use MUP units in either -- within the -- the corps or within -- I'm sorry, I withdraw that last part. Did your OG, OG Zapad, ever use MUP units in combat or in any other functions?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: How many times did you use MUP units in combat?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Several times, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What was the process whereby they were put under your command for use in combat?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in contact with the chief of the MUP, whose unit I would engage, and the chief would give his consent for the engagement of the unit and I was then free to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And what was the process whereby you gave them back to the chief of the MUP, that is, transferred the subordination back to the chief of the MUP? How did you do that?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Most often, when I tell the commander of the unit in combat that his mission was finished, he would go back to his chief, contact him, and that would mean that his engagement within my unit was finished.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Was that done verbally or in writing or in combination? What was the practice?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: What about the subordination of the MUP units to you in combat? Was that done verbally or in writing or in combination?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could also take place in combination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: To your knowledge, was the -- was there a practice in -- within the former Yugoslavia and the armies engaged in the various conflicts, ABiH, HV, VRS, HVO, VJ, to use MUP units in combats?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were in principle a component part of the armed forces during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Morrissey also asked you directly about the comparative strengths of the HVO and the ABiH and suggested that the HVO had a marked advantage in terms of tanks, shells, and materiel equipment; whereas, the ABiH had a -- an advantage in troop numbers. The HVO, he suggested -- I withdraw that. What was your knowledge of where the HVO was obtaining its tanks from?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, there can be no question of that arising out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you. That's beyond the scope of the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Your Honour, I may be about another ten minutes or so in -- in re-examination. I note the time. I wish to move to another topic. It's 27 past 10.00. Would this be an appropriate time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, maybe we could have a break, and we'll resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Re.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Mr. Cikotic, yesterday Mr. Morrissey asked you about the 6th -- the involvement of the 6th Corps and its units in Operation Neretva, and the question he specifically asked was: "And to your knowledge, Salko Gusic remained involved in the operation as commander of the 6th Corps as long as it lasted; is that correct?" To which your answer was: "That was my understanding." That's at page 57 of the transcript of yesterday in my printout. My questions of clarification in relation to that answer are the following: Did you have any contact -- personal contact with Salko Gusic during the days in which you were in combat in Operation Neretva?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't have any contacts with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge of what he was doing, he personally and physically, in the days in which you were in combat in your participation in Operation Neretva?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Are you aware during that same period who, if anyone, was issuing direct orders to the units which would have been under his control in the 6th Corps, at least before Operation Neretva?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know that. At the meeting at which I was given my mission, Salko Gusic was given his mission, and I assume that after that he continued his command role over the 6th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: My colleague Mr. Morrissey questioned you about subordination of the 6th Corps units and their be given -- their being given tasks in the same way that you were. This is at page 53 of yesterday's transcript. And then he asked you: "So bearing in mind the military principles that you're familiar with, had there been an offence committed by 6th Corps soldiers, that should have been investigated by the brigade and ultimately the 6th Corps military security; is that correct?" To which you responded: "It is." Were you aware whether the Operation Neretva had attached to it military security service units or military police units?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, can I just object to that question. As I understand the evidence, operations don't have such things attached to them at all. The question is whether Mr. Halilovic, his team, or the IKM had such units attached to them, rather than whether they attached in this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm certainly happy to clarify it in that manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Did you hear the reclarified question, Mr. Cikotic, that is: Were you aware whether Mr. Halilovic, the team, or the IKM, which were according to the Prosecution case within Operation Neretva, had attached to them military police or military security service units?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: On the issue of disciplining or investigation or the responsibility for the investigation of offences and in the context of the question Mr. Morrissey asked you about the 6th Corps and who should investigate offenses committed by the 6th Corps, my question is this: As an operational group commander, if units were subordinated to you for a specific operation, who would have the responsibility to investigate offenses committed -- allegedly committed by units subordinated to you as an OG commander during the period in which they were subordinated to you?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question is a hypothetical one, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Well, it could also be a concrete one. If, for example -- or if offences were committed by your units, the 307th or the 317th, for example, was it your responsibility as the commander of the operational group to investigate and punish offenses committed by subordinates of yours?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, that ought to be clarified. It's now said this is a concrete one. Is my learned friend putting to the witness that this happened, that -- that such units did commit offenses? Because he's used the term "a concrete one." So either it's hypothetical or it's not and it better be made clear what the situation is.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In my submission it doesn't matter because if it has happened, what did he or what should he have done, and if he didn't, in terms of subordination, who has the responsibility, whether it happened or not. It's a hypothetical question, but if he can answer it concretely, he's certainly entitled to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, maybe you should stick to the hypothetical question.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: In terms of your understanding of military law and doctrine, was it the responsibility of the operational group commander to discipline or investigate offenses committed by units under that person's control?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And if you were taking orders from Mr. Halilovic in relation to this operation, as you've given evidence of, and at that point were still organically within the 3rd Corps but under the command of Mr. Halilovic for that particular operation, if you, Mr. Cikotic, personally had committed an offense - for example, murdered a POW or shot some civilians - would it have been Mr. Halilovic's responsibility or someone else's to investigate - it's an open-ended question - Mr. Halilovic's responsibility or someone else's to investigate your alleged criminality and to punish you?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, there's a number of objections to that, but I'll -- I'll leave the main objection to it, and that is this question doesn't arise out of cross-examination. It's got a number of misleading clauses in it. Not deliberately, I don't suggest that. But -- and it's got some assumptions built into it too, which -- which the witness has not agreed to. If my friend wants to ask -- there's a question there that I wouldn't object to, frankly, although I don't want to be -- it's not meant to be a rude comment about it. I don't object to questions being asked to clarify the question that I asked when this witness said that the responsibility for military police and military investigations for the units subordinate -- the units that were subordinated to Operation Neretva 93, he said that responsibility remained with the 3rd Corps. And if my friend wants to ask the question: If this witness shot somebody in the head while in a -- in a particular hypothetical situation, then that may assist the Tribunal and I wouldn't object to it. But putting this in a sort of half hypothetical and half real way is just misleading, and it's -- the answer couldn't help anyone, frankly. So I'd -- I'd submit that if it's hypothetical, it's got to be clear and defined and -- I probably wouldn't object it to, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, yes, maybe you could put your question in another way.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm happy to put the question in another way, if it assist it is Trial Chamber's understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Yesterday Mr. Morrissey asked you directly about the investigation of crimes, if any, committed by your soldiers. The question was -- I put the question to you. He said: Question -- this is at page 52 of my printout: "And I want to put some propositions arising out of the" -- "out of that" meaning resubordination out of the organic structure of the 3rd Corps. "At all times you retained your links and responsibilities with regard to the 3rd Corps, with regard to logistic, military security, investigation of crimes, if any, by your soldiers, or matters outside of the combat activities of Neretva 93; is that accurate?" "Yes" -- Answer: "That's correct." "Now, I understand that none of your soldiers committed any outrages against civilians in the period we're talking about, but you being a commander on the spot there can tell us this. If one of your soldiers had been accused of suspecting of doing such a thing, the way you understood the structure that you operated under, that would have been investigated by the military security of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?" Answer: "The brigade where such a crime might have occurred and security services of the 3rd Corps." In the context of that question, what I'm asking you is your evidence has been that Mr. Halilovic commanded the operation and gave you orders --

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Just a minute. He -- never did he say that Mr. Halilovic commanded the operation. That's what the Prosecution have been hoping for for a long time. But that's just not what he said. He said he coordinated. My -- I object to this line of questioning, Your Honour. I think its true purpose has now been revealed. It doesn't -- it's not really re-examination at all. It's a -- it's another try and I object to it now in total.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: It's actually a clarification of that -- of that issue, as to who bore, if -- if the troops were subordinated, if Mr. Cikotic's OG was subordinated to Mr. Halilovic and Mr. Cikotic committed a crime or his troops committed a crime, would it have been Mr. Hadzihasanovic's responsibility or Mr. Halilovic's responsibility for crimes committed within that period. Now, that goes to the -- the heart of the allegations in the indictment. And it must arise out of cross-examination because he -- Mr. Morrissey asked a similar question. I want to clarify it by moving it to whether it's Mr. Hadzihasanovic or Mr. Halilovic. That has to - has to - come out of cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, you may ask a hypothetical question without mentioning any names. The issue is that we should make sure who has the responsibility to punish any crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If you committed a crime or troops under your control committed a crime, as Mr. Morrissey put to you hypothetically yesterday whilst still within the organic instruct of the 3rd Corps but following orders issued by Mr. Halilovic in relation to that operation, whose responsibility would it have been to punish you? The 3rd Corps commander or the person issuing the orders?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understood it, you gave clear guidance as to the sort of question that could be asked, and this question is not within that guideline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes. Don't mention any names.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: Withdrawing the name -- or withdrawing the positions, whose responsibility would it have been to punish you or to investigate?

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: That's -- Your Honour, this is just card playing now of -- that question simply says: "Withdrawing the names; answer exactly the question that I've just asked you."

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: The objection was -- the objection was as to names, so I'm saying who -- who was it? Anyone -- I mean, I can't be any less --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Well, let Mr. Morrissey finish. Let Mr. Morrissey finish.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORRISSEY
utterances.text: Your Honour, as I understand the position, what the Prosecutor is entitled to ask is as follows: If an -- and this is following the terms of his questions earlier. If an operations group were subordinated to a commander for an operation, who would be responsible for punishing the crimes? That's the type of hypothetical question as I understood my friend was endeavouring to ask, and it can be phrased in that neutral way. And I wouldn't object.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: I'm indebted to my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LIU
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: And I'll put the question in exactly those terms.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
utterances.text: If an operations group was subordinated to a commander for an operation, who would be responsible for punishing any crimes?

utterances.speaker: SELMO CIKOTIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the superior command, it would be the command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. RE
